# Phase directive — «A new CLI version stamped automatically» (Epoch 4, viola-0.2.0; the head entry at `816f9a77`)

**WHAT IS AN INPUT, AND WHAT IS NOT.** Of the folder this directive stands in, the ONLY files you read or snap are
this directive and the relay files a later send names. Nothing else under it is read, cited or snapped. A fact the
plan needs and this directive does not state is ASKED of the overseer in the P3 block, never looked up.

The operator is AWAY from THIS session (he answers through the overseer's dialogs, and he is at hand today): raise
NO question dialog for him. A fork that is his is written to `{run_dir}/founder-forks.md` (the question, the
options in order with each one's cost, the recommendation marked) and the step stops there, saying so. A technical
fork is answered by the overseer's relay at once. **This phase makes NO live start and reads nothing of the
operator's real `~/.claude*`.** In your chat messages name a compiled screen literal, never print it.

## Facts, measured by the overseer 2026-11-20 — cite them as this directive's

- **The founder's direction, his own words in the overseer's dialog (2026-11-20):** Claude Code updates almost
  daily, and the stamp should be set automatically when the host's version moves, because sorting it by hand
  each time is a burden; asked where the automation lives, he chose «В продукте Viola, отдельной записью» over a
  launcher script and over pinning the host's version. He was told in that dialog that any automatic form means
  his STANDING permission for one live verify per new version, with no question to him.
- **What moved, measured on this host:** PATH's `claude` went 2.1.326 → .327 → .328 → .329 in four days (mise
  `latest`). After each move a session started by `viola run` comes up `unverified-cli`: the driver's sends and
  answers are refused until a human runs `viola verify` for that version. Today a bare `claude` is 2.1.329 and no
  stamp of it stands anywhere; this session still runs 2.1.328, started before the move.
- The tree at `816f9a77` holds 27 relied ledger rows and ONE stamped fixture set (2.1.328); the live home's stamp is
  a 24-row stamp of 2.1.328 and the pinned product (the release build of `a59da9da`) is untouched until its
  re-pin. A 27-row stamp of 2.1.328 stands only in the rig's kept `target/live-rig/question-stamp.json`.
- The pinned product holds none of the last three mends: call no scheduled-wake or timer tool, and never print a
  compiled screen literal in a chat message.
- The documentation leaves hold no figure the code states: this chunk adds none.

## The directive

1. Scope is the route entry and its carries as they stand at `816f9a77`, nothing wider: a `viola run` that meets a
   `claude` version with no stamp gets that version stamped without a human running verify by hand. The WATCH on
   `cli_wheel path5_a_turn_left_running_is_cleared_by_pause_then_release` is read at each run — a recurrence is
   read from the job log and the test's own events BEFORE any mend; the rehearsal red is acted on only at its
   next red. Every carry is disposed by name in the plan.
2. **The size risk is the FORM, and it is the founder's.** Say at P3, from the code and with NO start:
   - how the version gate decides today (where the version is read, where the stamp is read, what `unverified-cli`
     refuses and what it still allows), and what `viola verify` is as a process: its runs, how long it takes (from
     the earlier chunks' ledgered starts in the store — quote the measured walls), every byte it types, every
     dialog it answers, what it writes and where, what it leaves in the user's Claude config (the transcripts
     residual), and what it SPENDS (model turns per verify, from the recorded runs);
   - each candidate form, with what it rests on and how it FAILS: verify run by `viola run` itself before the
     session starts (blocking the start for verify's wall) · verify run beside the session, the session starting
     unverified and turning verified when the stamp lands · a separate verb or flag the launcher calls · a config
     key that turns the automatic form on (off by default, or on) · any other the code offers. For each: who waits
     and how long, what the human sees, what a second `viola run` started meanwhile does (two verifies of one
     version at once — the stamp's writer and its lock), and what happens offline or with no login;
   - **a RED verify of a new version — the case that matters most:** the product must not loop (a verify on every
     start of a version that failed), must say plainly which rows failed, and must leave the session to the human
     as today. Say where a failed attempt is recorded so it is not repeated, and what clears it (a newer viola
     build, a newer row set, a human's `viola verify`);
   - **the spend and the consent:** an automatic verify spends the user's model turns and writes a stamp in the
     user's REAL viola home with no human in the loop. Say what the product asks or tells the user before the
     first one (a config key he sets once; a line printed each time), and what a user who never wants it does;
   - what the existing rows say today about who starts verify and when: **search ALL seven masters before the
     block is written** (verify's start, «stamps are written only by verify», the version gate, `unverified-cli`,
     exit 12, the config keys' closed set, the residual rows, the driver-permission rows, what `viola run` may
     spawn) and name EVERY reached row in the block, with the ones read as not reached beside them. A widening is
     said as one HERE, whole;
   - how it is PROVED: over the fake agent (a version with no stamp → the automatic verify → verified; a red one
     → recorded and not repeated; two runs at once), and whether ANY live start is wanted — 2.1.329 stands on this
     host unstamped, so a live reading would be the product stamping it in a SCRATCH viola home under the rig,
     never in the live home; say its shape before its count;
   - whether one implement window holds it, or the entry splits and where.
3. **At P3's END, before P4, stop with ONE block in `founder-forks.md`:** your window; the form recommended and
   the ones set aside, each with how it fails; the red-verify behaviour; the consent form and its default; every
   reached master row; every live start's SHAPE before the count — processes, every byte typed, every dialog and
   how it is answered, the stop, every file written and where, under WHICH home; for each start a predicate its
   reading can FAIL, the red reading named; what each start READS and from WHERE; whether any typed key or
   answered dialog moves the wheel before a send; the capability's concretized claim, if one is claimed, and what
   «verified» would rest on; a recommended cap and what one spare would be for. The form, the default, the spend,
   the cap, any key or byte into a CLI dialog, any widening and any read or write under his real home are the
   founder's: the block WAITS for him.
4. **For every capped start, name what it needs ABSENT or PRESENT on disk outside the tree,** each with a no-start
   gate entry right before the start — or written as true by construction WITH its code line. Never write that
   the rig refuses a condition without the line that refuses it.
5. One ledger, one count: `--cap` is the RUNNING total of base starts in the ledger file. A census entry after
   the LAST live leg is keyed to the operator leg. **An entry that asserts a state a LATER step of the same plan
   ends is keyed to the round leg,** so the wrap's light gate does not fire it.
6. Every control stands on an entry filtered to its guard's own cases, or its record names the guard's own case
   as failed and lists any other; the bound that applies is the entry's own timeout key, ids within 16
   characters. Every filter term of a gate entry SELECTS at least one test under its layer flag. An expect atom
   must be able to fail; a word that may honestly read two ways is a READING recorded. A test that skips prints
   its reason. The plan names operator entries by their run text, never by a number.
7. Before a live round the host is read (`hostwatch.py read --last 15`): a CONTENDED reading with a NEIGHBOUR
   named stops and is re-read, never retried into. The token window is the rig's own check, never a hand read.
8. No mutation run. A test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint — a rehearsal of an automatic verify does
   not sleep out a real one. Every TEST start runs under a test-owned user home. Read `df` before a whole
   rebuild.
9. A fold is decided at the PHASE. A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop
   and tell the overseer. On an account-limit refusal, stop where you are.
10. Call NO scheduled-wake or timer tool, with any argument. End every process you start; remove no scratch
    clone by a recursive delete — name it on the card instead.
11. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the
    union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; whether EVERY cited row is in the union or its standing
    list; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` / `INDETERMINATE` /
    `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.

2. **`crates/viola-state/src/stamps.rs` — `try_verify_lock(home)`, the attempt lock.**
   - Order:
     1. `strict::check_stamps` runs first, before anything is made (`(security-plan · decision/stamps-strict-check-first)`).
     2. `create_private_dir(ledger_dir)`.
     3. `open_private_lock(ledger/verify.lock)`, the same helper as `stamps.json.lock` (stamps.rs:64).
     4. `File::try_lock`.
   - It returns `Ok(Some(guard))` with the lock held until drop, `Ok(None)` when another process holds it, and
     `Err(StampsError::StrictModes)` with nothing made or narrowed.
   - It never blocks, and it never takes `stamps.json.lock`, which verify's `update_stamps` takes (stamps.rs:57-70):
     holding that one across verify would deadlock its own child.
   - Unit cases:
     - `try_verify_lock_takes_a_free_lock` (`ledger/` 0700, the lock 0600);
     - `try_verify_lock_reads_a_held_lock_as_none` (a second open of the same file holding it);
     - `try_verify_lock_frees_on_drop`;
     - `try_verify_lock_refuses_a_widened_ledger_and_leaves_it`, the mode read back unchanged (tests history n=27).
   - The file is P4-F2's subject.

4. **`schemas/diag-line.v1.json:116` — the `subject` enum gains `auto-verify`.** It is additive
   (`(obs-plan · decision/diag-schema-additive-only)`; obs history n=5, n=16).

5. **`src/run/version_gate.rs` — the gate also names what it read for the version.**
   - `Gate` gains a closed field, `entry`, with three values:
     - `Unusable`: no version parsed, or the read refused, unreadable or malformed;
     - `Unattempted`: no stamps file, no entry, or an entry `!attempted`;
     - `Attempted`.
   - `cli_verified`, the `parse-rejected{ledger-stamps}` lines, the `version-probe` pair and the `run.version_gate`
     span are unchanged.
   - A refused, unreadable or malformed ledger is never read as a missing stamp (obs history n=4).
   - Unit case `gate_entry_reads_every_arm`, beside `stamps_verdict_reads_every_arm`, covers six arms: absent file,
     no entry, short entry, attempted green, attempted red, malformed.

6. **`src/run/auto_verify.rs` (new) — the start's automatic verify.**
   - It carries NO `#[instrument]`: its lines ride `run.start`'s span, so
     `(obs-plan · contract/run-start-spans/span-chain)` holds unchanged. Events go through `obs_event!` only.
   - **The decision**, a pure `decide(key, &Gate) -> Step`:
     - key off, no version, verified, or `Unusable` → `Nothing`;
     - `Attempted` and not verified → `EarlierRed`;
     - `Unattempted` → `Verify`.
     - Unit table `decide_reads_every_arm`. Its `entry_short_of_one_relied_id` case is the «verifies again once» proof
       (founder-forks §6), since no booted test may hand-write a short stamp (tests history n=25).
   - **`EarlierRed`:** line L3, and the gate is returned unchanged.
   - **`Verify`:**
     1. `try_verify_lock`: `Ok(None)` → line L4, unverified. `Err` → line L5 with `lock-refused`, unverified.
     2. Under the lock, `read_stamps_strict` again. If the entry now reads `Attempted` (another start just finished),
        its verdict is taken and no verify runs.
     3. Otherwise line L1, then the spawn.
   - **The spawn:**
     - the command is `<pinned copy> --home <canonical home> verify -- <the start's resolved program>`, with no user
       argument. The gate's `--version` takes none either (version_gate.rs:146).
     - The pinned copy is `Pinned.path`, whose bytes the start checked
       (`(security-plan · decision/start-pins-the-bytes-it-checked)`).
     - cwd: the start's own process cwd, as a hand-run verify's.
     - stdin: null (security history n=12: never the human's stdin).
     - stdout and stderr are inherited, or null when `launch.json` (revive `--json`, below).
     - env: the start's own `StripPlan` applied (security history n=41), and `VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR` and
       `VIOLA_BIN` removed, so verify writes no process log of its own (`src/cmd/verify.rs:66-67`) and stamps only
       the `--home` it is given.
     - It is a direct spawn, never a shell.
     - `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` is `SIGTERM` in `pre_exec`, set from the start's own thread, so a killed start never leaves
       its verify running (tests history n=52–n=53).
     - One `process-start` / `process-exit` pair with subject `auto-verify`, carrying `child_exit_status` and
       `duration_ms`, the version-probe pair's shape (version_gate.rs:150-170).
   - **The wait:**
     - `try_wait` every 10 ms, with no deadline of its own: verify bounds every child itself (`PROBE_DEADLINE`, the
       typed runs' deadlines).
     - A stop flag is set by a `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` handler, installed only for the wait. It takes the form of
       `src/cmd/verify/stop.rs`, an async-signal-safe store.
   - **The stop** (`inputs#I2` item 6):
     1. TERM to the verify child (verify ends its own child with no key and removes its dirs, `verify/stop.rs`).
     2. Wait for it up to `STOP_GRACE` = 30 s, then KILL.
     3. Write the pair's `process-exit`.
     4. Restore `SIG_DFL` for that signal and raise it.

     The start ends the way a start interrupted today ends: by the signal. No snapshot, no child, no document, no new
     exit code (`(architecture · decision/retired-exit-codes-never-reused)`). The lock is dropped by the exit, and no
     stamp is written, so the next start tries again.
   - **After a verify that exits:**
     - `read_stamps_strict` again;
     - `Attempted` and verified → the gate turns verified;
     - `Attempted` and not verified → line L2;
     - otherwise → line L5 with `unstamped`;
     - a spawn error → line L5 with `spawn-failed`.
   - The lock is dropped after the re-read.
   - **Under `launch.json`** (revive `--json`), verify's stdout and stderr are null and no line is printed, so the
     closed `--json` documents stay exact (`(a11y-plan · contract/viola-revive-json/start-refusal)`). The outcome
     reaches the log pair and the stamp alone.
   - Unit cases:
     - `decide_reads_every_arm`;
     - `spawn_of_a_missing_exe_is_spawn_failed_with_nothing_written` (a non-existent pinned path: the word, no stamps
       file, the lock free after);
     - `silence_under_json_prints_no_line` (the line writer over a `Vec`).

7. **`src/cmd/run.rs` `start` — the place in the order.**
   - New order: `version_gate` (run.rs:290), then `bind_endpoint` (run.rs:293), then `auto_verify`, then
     `trust_folder` with the FINAL verdict, then everything after.
   - The automatic verify comes after the bind so that a refused socket directory still refuses «before any
     snapshot, child or bind», with no verify child spawned. This holds
     `(security-plan · decision/start-checks-socket-dir-before-bind)` and its layouts and a11y twins, and it refines
     §2(A)'s place (founder-forks.md, P4's «read as NOT reached»).
   - During verify the endpoint is bound and not served. No snapshot names it yet, so no client reaches it, and a
     second start of the same name reads `squatted-name` as today.
   - The final `Gate` feeds unchanged code:
     - `SendSlot::new` (run.rs:312);
     - `DialogSlot::new` (run.rs:328);
     - `start_state` (run.rs:354);
     - `Launched` (run.rs:617).
   - The doc comment of the start order (run.rs:258) names the new step.
   - `revive`'s start reaches it through the same `start` (src/cmd/revive.rs:154; arch history n=10).

8. **`src/human/auto_verify.rs` (new, declared in `src/human.rs`) — the start's five fixed lines.**
   - Each is one stderr write, ASCII, no SGR, never wrapped, holding only the parsed version `X.Y.Z` and a closed word
     (`(design-system · decision/cli-ascii-only)`, `(design-system · decision/lines-never-wrapped)`).
   - The lines:
     - L1 `verifying claude <version> once before the session: viola verify runs now`
     - L2 `claude <version> did not verify: this session starts unverified; run viola verify to try again`
     - L3 `claude <version> failed viola verify on an earlier start: this session starts unverified; run viola verify to try again`
     - L4 `claude <version> is being verified by another start: this session starts unverified`
     - L5 `viola verify ended without a stamp (<word>): this session starts unverified`, where `<word>` is one of
       `spawn-failed` · `unstamped` · `lock-refused`

title: D. The whole green, then the live round

data.head: ### D. The whole green, then the live round

body:
24. **The workspace layers:** `run --unit`, `--integration` and `--e2e`, then the boot smoke. All are green before
    the round (`inputs#I1` item 9).

25. **Read the host first:** `python3 ~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py
    read --last 15`, by hand. The verdict line goes to `evidence/live-round.md`.
    - A CONTENDED reading naming a NEIGHBOUR stops: re-read later, never retried into (`inputs#I1` item 7).
    - The token window is the rig's own check.

26. **The round** (`gate.py run --chunk 2026-11-20-a-new-cli-version-stamped-automatically --run-dir {implement run dir}
    --live-legs`) fires in block order:
    1. PATH's `claude` read for its version and its install by path;
    2. the census;
    3. the plain build with its hash;
    4. the live home's stamps sha, recorded once;
    5. the runtime dir read owner-only;
    6. `AV`.

    **The no-start conditions** (`inputs#I1` item 4; `inputs#I2` item 10), each an entry right before the start or
    true by construction with its code line:
    - **The scratch viola home ABSENT before — BY CONSTRUCTION.**
      - Each start makes `<scratch base>/<run>`, where `<run>` is the rig's own pid and OS start time
        (`crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/procs.rs:64-68`, called at `mod.rs:552`).
      - Its `vhome/` is made inside that fresh root (`crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs:409-421`).
      - The base `/tmp/viola-rig-<uid>` (isolate.rs:35-38) lies on tmpfs.
      - Named limit: `create_private_dir` admits a standing dir, so freshness rests on the run id, not on a refusal.
    - **The live home's stamps sha — an ENTRY before** (written once), **and one AFTER** (unmoved).
    - **`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` owner-only — an ENTRY, right before `AV`.** The wrapped arm keeps it for its `viola run`
      (`crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs:24-32`).
    - **The kept record or stamp:** none. `AV` keeps neither.
    - **The cap ledger** `evidence/auto-starts.ndjson` is appended by design; its base lines ARE the cap
      (`inputs#I1` item 5).
    - **The CI refusal:** the rig's live arm refuses under `CI` before its ledger line
      (`crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs:457-459`).

27. **`AV` = the founder's ONE base start** (`inputs#I2` item 4):
    - It runs against PATH's version, read right before the start inside the same entry. If mise has moved past
      2.1.329, the start goes against whatever unstamped version stands there (`inputs#I2` item 10).
    - Processes: `viola run` → its `--version` → `viola verify` (one `--version`, the Haiku print probe, six PTY runs,
      one agents read) → the session's `claude` (`--model haiku`). That is up to 11 `claude` processes, at most two at
      once.
    - Typed bytes: only verify's compiled pastes; the rig types no key; nothing is sent to the session.
    - Dialogs: only Runs C and D's, answered by the capture hook's closed ids. No byte goes into any CLI dialog.
    - From the real home, `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is read once (a 0600 copy, removed on every exit path).
      Nothing is written under the real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`.
    - **GREEN** only on the founder's predicate: `stamp-ids: all` (PATH's version's entry carries every relied id),
      `verdict-match: yes`, `auto-verify-pairs: 1`, plus the teardown words.
    - `stamp-verdict` and `failing` are READINGS. A 2.1.329 that drifts on a row is the product working, and the
      version stays unverified.
    - The spare `AV-2` is spent only for a host CONTENDED by a neighbour or a rig fault BEFORE verify's first spawn,
      never to re-roll a red reading. A second base start is the founder's.

28. **Right after:** the census keyed `operator`, then the live stamps sha read unmoved.
    - A red `AV` (an atom of the predicate or a teardown word) stops implement before the operator pass. The rig
      summary is recorded whole in `evidence/live-round.md`, with the cause in the summary's own words.
- `src/run/auto_verify.rs` — the key reader, `decide`, the attempt, the verify child, its stop, the re-read
- `src/human/auto_verify.rs` — the start's five fixed lines and their writer
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — `attempted` beside `verified`
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_stamps.rs` — the `attempted` table
- `crates/viola-state/src/stamps.rs` — `try_verify_lock` and its unit cases
- `src/obs.rs` — `CONFIG_KEYS` gains `verify_new_cli`; its unit case's key list
- `schemas/config.v1.json` — the `verify_new_cli` boolean property
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` — the `auto-verify` subject
- `src/run/version_gate.rs` — `Gate.entry` and its unit case
- `src/run/mod.rs` — declares `auto_verify`
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — the step after the bind, `trust_folder` on the final verdict, the order comment
- `src/human.rs` — declares `auto_verify`
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — `fake-args` beside the executable, prepended to argv
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/test_cases_opts.rs` — the `fake-args` case
- `tests/support/fake.rs` — `write_fake_args`
- `tests/cli_version_gate.rs` — cases 11–16
- `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs` — the `verify_new_cli` row and its rstest
- `tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs` — the `config.json verify_new_cli` boundary
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` — `Arm::AV`, its labels, summary lines, cases
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs` — `AV`'s vhome seed with the key
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs` — the usage line names `AV`
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` — the `AV` rehearsal pair
The block runs in this order:
- **Phase A:** the formatter, the linter, the agent crate's cases, the state crate's cases, the root bin's cases.
- **Phase B:** the two filtered control entries.
- **Phase C:** the rig library cases, then the rehearsal pair.
- **Phase E:** the operator pass.
What is not run, and why:
- No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 8).

- No release check entry: CI's `release` job runs `scripts/release-check.sh` on the push, and no new binary or feature
  is added.
- The fake agent's `fake-args` is test-only code in a `fake-agent` binary.

Bounds and homes: every test start runs under its test-owned home and user home (tests S1). The live start runs under
the rig's private scratch at `/tmp/viola-rig-<uid>/`, and the rig's `--deadline` bounds it under the entry's `timeout`.
`AV` is ledgered in `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-20-a-new-cli-version-stamped-automatically/evidence/auto-starts.ndjson`.
`--cap` is the running total of base lines in that one file (`inputs#I1` item 5).

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries (validation.md check
4 (6)).
- Each fires on an entry filtered to its own case alone (`inputs#I1` item 6).

- Each reads «holds» only when its named case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line. Its record lists every case that
  failed in the removed run.
| | `attempted-arm` | `verify-lock` |
| **File** | `src/run/auto_verify.rs` | `src/run/auto_verify.rs` |

| **The edit removes** | `decide`'s `EarlierRed` arm, so an `Attempted` unverified entry reads `Verify` (implement quotes the exact text in the control record) | the `Ok(None)` arm of the lock's match, so a held lock goes on to verify as if taken (implement quotes the exact text) |

| **Case** | `verify_window_run_whose_verify_goes_red_records_it_and_the_next_start_runs_none` (start 2 counts one `auto-verify` line, not zero) | `verify_window_two_starts_at_once_run_one_verify` (B runs a verify: two `auto-verify` starts) |
| **Fired on** | the entry filtered to that case, `--timeout 600` | the entry filtered to that case, `--timeout 600` |
| **A timeout reads as** | not held: the case must FAIL | not held |

6. **`src/run/auto_verify.rs` (new) — the start's automatic verify.**
   - It carries NO `#[instrument]`: its lines ride `run.start`'s span, so
     `(obs-plan · contract/run-start-spans/span-chain)` holds unchanged. Events go through `obs_event!` only.
   - **The decision**, a pure `decide(key, &Gate) -> Step`:
     - key off, no version, verified, or `Unusable` → `Nothing`;
     - `Attempted` and not verified → `EarlierRed`;
     - `Unattempted` → `Verify`.
     - Unit table `decide_reads_every_arm`. Its `entry_short_of_one_relied_id` case is the «verifies again once» proof
       (founder-forks §6), since no booted test may hand-write a short stamp (tests history n=25).
   - **`EarlierRed`:** line L3, and the gate is returned unchanged.
   - **`Verify`:**
     1. `try_verify_lock`: `Ok(None)` → line L4, unverified. `Err` → line L5 with `lock-refused`, unverified.
     2. Under the lock, `read_stamps_strict` again. If the entry now reads `Attempted` (another start just finished),
        its verdict is taken and no verify runs.
     3. Otherwise line L1, then the spawn.
   - **The spawn:**
     - the command is `<pinned copy> --home <canonical home> verify -- <the start's resolved program>`, with no user
       argument. The gate's `--version` takes none either (version_gate.rs:146).
     - The pinned copy is `Pinned.path`, whose bytes the start checked
       (`(architecture · decision/start-pins-the-bytes-it-checked)`, looked up by `rec.py find`).
     - cwd: the start's own process cwd, as a hand-run verify's.
     - stdin: null (security history n=12: never the human's stdin).
     - stdout and stderr are inherited, or null when `launch.json` (revive `--json`, below).
     - env: the start's own `StripPlan` applied (security history n=41), and `VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR` and
       `VIOLA_BIN` removed, so verify writes no process log of its own (`src/cmd/verify.rs:66-67`) and stamps only
       the `--home` it is given.
     - It is a direct spawn, never a shell.
     - `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` is `SIGTERM` in `pre_exec`, set from the start's own thread, so a killed start never leaves
       its verify running (tests history n=52–n=53).
     - One `process-start` / `process-exit` pair with subject `auto-verify`, carrying `child_exit_status` and
       `duration_ms`, the version-probe pair's shape (version_gate.rs:150-170).
   - **The wait:**
     - `try_wait` every 10 ms, with no deadline of its own: verify bounds every child itself (`PROBE_DEADLINE`, the
       typed runs' deadlines).
     - A stop flag is set by a `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` handler, installed only for the wait. It takes the form of
       `src/cmd/verify/stop.rs`, an async-signal-safe store.
   - **The stop** (`inputs#I2` item 6):
     1. TERM to the verify child (verify ends its own child with no key and removes its dirs, `verify/stop.rs`).
     2. Wait for it up to `STOP_GRACE` = 30 s, then KILL.
     3. Write the pair's `process-exit`.
     4. Restore `SIG_DFL` for that signal and raise it.

     The start ends the way a start interrupted today ends: by the signal. No snapshot, no child, no document, no new
     exit code (`(architecture · decision/retired-exit-codes-never-reused)`). The lock is dropped by the exit, and no
     stamp is written, so the next start tries again.
   - **After a verify that exits:**
     - `read_stamps_strict` again;
     - `Attempted` and verified → the gate turns verified;
     - `Attempted` and not verified → line L2;
     - otherwise → line L5 with `unstamped`;
     - a spawn error → line L5 with `spawn-failed`.
   - The lock is dropped after the re-read.
   - **Under `launch.json`** (revive `--json`), verify's stdout and stderr are null and no line is printed, so the
